doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Building jazz education in Hanoi
summary: Rydin has worked in Vietnam eight or nine times, teaching teachers and administrators, performing, using a translator.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What I also have done, which I’m happy to be doing, is I’ve been working quite a lot in Hanoi, in Vietnam, helping them to build their jazz education. And now they have jazz

education with lots of students and lots of piano players. In fact I’m going there again next week but I’ve been there I think eight or nine times and I’ve been working like a month at a time at the academy teaching and working with the administration, how to give good education and teaching the teachers, and playing, performing. So I’ve got a lot of friends there and I perform there quite a lot.
And what language do you communicate in?
English of course, but I have to have a translator most of the time because not all of them know English. So it takes a little time.
